hypotheses.claim: program-301 terrain shading differs by a smooth scalar factor (fog/lighting path)
hypotheses.evidence: first divergence is the first terrain draw; 95% of differing pixels are 1 LSB and alpha never differs; per-channel fit delta=a+b*value shows land as an almost pure scalar multiplier (0.18-0.27% relative) and water with an additional channel-dependent component; differing fraction is higher in smooth regions (66.6%) than detailed regions (56.3%) and the error autocorrelation is broad and smooth with no texel-scale or periodic peak, which refutes texture filtering as the dominant mechanism; textures, index/position buffers and UNIFORM1 are identical to the byte-exact canonical frame, only the engine uniform block differs

gl_control.method: seed the captured pre-draw GL image, replay one captured draw through a legacy CGL OpenGL context with the captured GLSL, attribute/index blobs, texture levels, sampler state, uniforms and GL state, read back
gl_control.interpretation: the Metal replay reproduces the captured inputs almost exactly as OpenGL does; both differ from the live GL frame on the same pixels in the same direction, so the divergence is introduced by the captured inputs, not by Metal translation
gl_control.candidate_lossy_input: compressed textures are captured as glGetTexImage RGBA8 readbacks, so both replays sample the readback decode instead of the sampler decode; the canonical menu-occ300 frame replays byte-exactly, so the loss is content-dependent
gl_control.limits: single-sample FBO versus the reference multisampled default framebuffer; depth cleared to 1.0 (the <=1152 px painted by event 14 are excluded from sensitivity); textures are the captured decompressed payloads by design
